stimuli.description: Six environmental conditions combining specific light (warm 3500K/350lx, cool 6500K/830lx, flickering 3500K/50-830lx) and sound (silent, white noise 40dB, classroom noise 75dB) settings.
Moving target fractions (MTF) task presented on a screen, requiring participants to identify and click on fractions greater than one-half.
Sound conditions included silence, white noise at 40 dB, and classroom noise at 75 dB.

limitations: Increasing the number of participants and including individuals from various age ranges and cultural backgrounds would enhance the diversity and generalizability of our findings.

Gathering qualitative feedback from participants through open-ended surveys or semi-structured interviews could enrich our insights and potentially reveal factors impacting the individual's perceived experience that sensors might not capture.
Measuring the peak wavelength of light during the experiment is helpful for understanding the non-visual effects of light, providing a more comprehensive analysis of its impact.
The use of the EEG cap can introduce some level of discomfort for participants which itself could influence the results.
EEG is highly sensitive to movement, we asked participants to minimize abrupt movements as much as possible.
The deployment of EEG in a real-world situation is currently time-consuming, costly, and requires expertise.
This work, however, should be considered as a primary study with a limited set of conditions.
